solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Film with outfit's central characters kept in intense church and domestic surroundings?

parts.note: pic is a short informal word for a film or picture

indicators.note: kept in says one piece is held inside another

parts.note: intense means keen, as in keen interest

indicators.note: the central characters are the middle letters of the word outfit

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A cinema-goer describes a film about a fervent churchgoing family, with costumes at its heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central characters' of outfit are TF, 'kept in' KEEN gives KETFEN. The question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A white paling fence is the classic boundary around an American house and garden, so it surrounds the domestic scene.

clue.text: Soldier not associated with the state

definitions.meaning: a soldier of the lowest rank in the army
owned or run by individuals rather than the government, as in a privately run company

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the lowest army rank and anything belonging to individuals rather than public bodies.

clue.text: Clubs getting award probed by Western book in fragile cover?

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

indicators.note: probed by says the award has another piece pushed into it

parts.note: the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A card player's prize is examined by a Western reader of a book with a delicate jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'probed by' puts W inside OBE to make OWBE. The OBE is a British state honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A spider's web is a flimsy veil draped over neglected objects, so it is a fragile covering, hence the question mark.

clue.text: People registered to make a crossing?

definitions.text: People registered to make a crossing?

parts.words: People registered to make a crossing?
parts.note: the crossing is not a road crossing but the cross a voter marks on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: Pedestrians signed up for a supervised road crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: Making a crossing suggests walking across a road; here it means putting an X on a ballot paper.
explanation.definitionFit: The registered voters of a country or constituency are those entitled to mark a cross on a ballot.

clue.text: Panic in fighter on circuit

parts.note: F designates a fighter aircraft, as in F-16
a lap is one circuit of a racetrack

explanation.surface: A fighter pilot loses his nerve while flying round a circuit.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts F above LAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a flap is an informal idiom for a state of agitated alarm or fluster.

clue.text: Nothing to represent amateur in big race? It's speculative

indicators.note: to represent says one letter stands in for another in the word

parts.note: the Grand National is Britain's famous steeplechase
O, the round zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: An amateur rider with nothing to show in the Grand National; his chances are speculative.
explanation.walkthrough: The Grand National is a famous British horse race; O replaces the first A.
explanation.definitionFit: Something notional exists only as an idea or hypothesis, which is to say it is speculative.

clue.text: Old Greek vessel right away mounted on island for retired academics

indicators.note: in a down clue mounted means the letters are read upwards, so backwards
away says a letter is removed from the ship's name

parts.note: a trireme was an ancient Greek galley with three banks of oars

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek ship mounted on an island display for retired professors to admire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' drops one R from the galley, and 'mounted' reads the rest upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Professors emeriti keep their title in retirement; this is the Latin plural of the honorary rank.

clue.text: Short gibe and incoherent talk a bishop disregarded making little objection

indicators.note: short says the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a quip is a witty gibe or remark

indicators.note: disregarded says these letters are left out of the word

parts.note: babble is confused, meaningless talk
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A barbed remark and rambling chatter, the bishop ignored, amounting to a petty complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: QUIP 'short' gives QUI; BABBLE with A and a B 'disregarded' leaves BBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A quibble is a minor, petty point of criticism, a small objection about trivial detail.

clue.text: Measure taken by royal on ground — and part of ship

parts.note: a quart is a measure of liquid volume
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen
the deck is slang for the ground or floor, as in hit the deck

explanation.surface: A royal personage takes a measurement on the ground, and also on part of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: ER = Queen is a crossword staple; 'hit the deck' gives deck = ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised rear deck of a vessel, traditionally reserved for officers, is one section of a ship.

clue.text: Banter exchanged about a nocturnal creature

indicators.note: about says the scrambled word goes round the single letter
exchanged says the letters of banter swap places

explanation.surface: Light-hearted chat traded about a night-time animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchanged' turns BANTER into ANTBER, which goes 'about' A.
explanation.definitionFit: The aardvark, also known by this name, is an African mammal that feeds on termites at night.

clue.text: Slowing recovery mostly noted after turmoil with a final bit of inflation set in

indicators.note: mostly says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a rally is a recovery, as of prices or health

indicators.note: set in says the extra letters are placed inside the scrambled word
turmoil says the letters of noted are thrown into disorder
the final bit of inflation is its last letter

explanation.surface: An economic recovery is mostly noted after a period of turmoil, with a little inflation setting in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slowing' is a musical direction, not economics; 'turmoil' scrambles the letters and 'set in' slips A and N inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: This musical direction tells the performer to slow down gradually, so it means slowing.

clue.text: Welsh politician recalled excessive time getting alcoholic preparation

parts.note: AM was an Assembly Member of the Welsh Assembly

indicators.note: recalled says the following words are read backwards

parts.note: OTT is over the top, excessive
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A Welsh politician remembered drinking too much of an alcoholic concoction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns OTTERA round to ARETTO.
explanation.definitionFit: This almond-flavoured Italian liqueur is a prepared alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Cheery work, draining black bottle

indicators.note: draining says a letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a job is a piece of work
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a vial is a small bottle

explanation.surface: A cheerful task: emptying a dark bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: JOB 'draining' B leaves JO.
explanation.definitionFit: Jovial describes a hearty, good-humoured and cheerful manner.

clue.text: A graduate invading city facilities creating uproar

indicators.note: invading says these letters push into the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: Hull is a port city in Yorkshire, England
the facilities is a euphemism for the toilet, the loo
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts graduate

explanation.surface: A graduate barges into a city's toilets, causing a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: Hull is a port city in Yorkshire, England; 'invading' puts the graduate between the city and the toilets.
explanation.definitionFit: A hullabaloo is a noisy fuss or commotion, the same as an uproar.

clue.text: River in wood precluding a long trip

indicators.note: in says the letter goes inside the shortened wood
precluding says the letter is shut out of the word

parts.note: teak is a hardwood timber

explanation.surface: A river in a forest ruling out a lengthy expedition.
explanation.walkthrough: TEAK 'precluding' A gives TEK, with R 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A trek is an arduous journey, especially a long one on foot.

clue.text: Distress I must rate possible when harbouring first sign of ailment

indicators.note: when harbouring says the scrambled letters hold another inside
possible says one arrangement of these letters is wanted
the first sign of ailment is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A patient worried at having to rate any symptoms of illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possible' rearranges IMUSTRATE, which 'when harbouring' takes A inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To traumatise is to cause someone severe emotional shock, which is to distress them.

clue.text: One bound to turn up consumed by drink having left dad outside

indicators.note: consumed by says one piece is swallowed inside the other
having left says the father figure departs from the drink's name

parts.note: an alcopop is a sweet fizzy alcoholic drink
pop is an informal word for dad

indicators.note: in a down clue to turn up means read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a serf was a labourer bound to a lord's land

explanation.surface: A feudal labourer turns up drunk after his father has left the house.
explanation.walkthrough: ALCOPOP without POP gives ALCO; SERF 'to turn up' gives FRES, 'consumed by' ALCO.
explanation.definitionFit: Eating al fresco means eating in the open air, outdoors.

clue.text: Retrograde dropout left blocking smart girl leaving college in determined fashion

indicators.note: retrograde means moving backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a loser is a failure or dropout

indicators.note: blocking says the letter sits in the middle, obstructing the word
leaving says a letter departs from the word

parts.note: a cutey is an attractive, smart-looking girl

explanation.surface: A backward-looking dropout stops a bright young woman abandoning her college studies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retrograde' makes RESOL; CUTEY 'leaving' C gives UTEY, with L 'blocking' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting resolutely means acting with firm purpose and resolve, in a determined way.

clue.text: Tiresome journey in southern Switzerland by lake with uphill course

parts.note: CH is the international code for Switzerland, from Confoederatio Helvetica

indicators.note: in a down clue uphill means the letters climb, so they read backwards

parts.note: PPE, Philosophy, Politics and Economics, is a university degree course at Oxford

explanation.surface: A weary hike in the south of Switzerland, past a lake and up a steep course.
explanation.walkthrough: PPE is a well-known Oxford degree course; 'uphill' reverses it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A schlepp, from Yiddish, is a tedious and arduous trip or slog.

clue.text: Group bordering a parliamentary constituency

indicators.note: bordering says one word surrounds the other on both sides

parts.note: a set is a group of things or people

explanation.surface: A group living on the edge of an electoral district.
explanation.walkthrough: SET 'bordering' A.
explanation.definitionFit: An MP's seat is the electoral district they represent in parliament.

clue.text: Clear couple of notes and another featuring in pared-down musical

indicators.note: featuring in says these letters appear inside the shortened show
pared-down says the show's title loses its last letter

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber and Rice musical about Eva Peron
D and E are two consecutive notes of the musical scale
N stands for note, giving one more

explanation.surface: Clear musical notes ring out in a trimmed production of a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: EVITA 'pared-down' is EVIT; DEN goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Evident means plainly visible or obvious, so clear in the sense of apparent.

clue.text: Festival traditional group promoted is captured by artist

indicators.note: captured by says the artist holds the group inside

parts.note: Salvador Dali was the Spanish surrealist painter

indicators.note: in a down clue promoted means raised, so the letters read upwards

parts.note: the WI, the Women's Institute, is a traditional British women's organisation

explanation.surface: A traditional society, promoted, is taken in by an artist at a festival.
explanation.walkthrough: The Women's Institute is a long-standing British women's organisation; 'promoted' reads it upwards in this down entry before the painter takes it in.
explanation.definitionFit: Diwali is the Hindu festival of lights celebrated each autumn.

clue.text: Egg on face of husband: former wife must be accommodated first or start to talk

indicators.note: this word only joins the neighbouring pieces: it says which one stands next to which in the answer

parts.note: an ex is a former wife

indicators.note: the face of husband is its first letter

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the start to talk is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A husband with egg on his face must make room for his ex-wife or start to talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egg on face' looks like embarrassment, but 'Egg on' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhort is to urge someone strongly, to encourage or egg them on.

clue.text: International no 6 must get into shape needing trim — recall could be hindered by it?

definitions.text: recall could be hindered by it?

indicators.note: must get into says these letters are inserted in the trimmed shape
needing trim says the last letter of the shape is cut

parts.note: an oblong is a rectangular shape
number six is VI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A sporting international, shirt number six, must get into shape and slim down.
explanation.walkthrough: OBLONG 'needing trim' is OBLON; IVI 'must get into' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblivion is the state of forgetting, which is what obstructs memory.

clue.text: Old walkway with section from Patras to Athens

indicators.note: section from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An ancient colonnade spanning the road from Patras to Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoa was a covered colonnade in ancient Greece, a sheltered walkway.

clue.text: Joint containing sandwiches with deficient contents and little sign of tasty diet?

indicators.note: containing says the joint holds the other letters

parts.note: the knee is a joint of the leg

indicators.note: with deficient contents says the word loses its middle, keeping only its ends
a little sign of tasty is its first letter

explanation.surface: A joint of meat stuffed with meagre sandwiches, hardly a tasty diet.
explanation.walkthrough: Diet here is not food but a legislative assembly; the question mark flags it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Israel's parliament is an example of a legislative assembly, which is one sense of diet.

clue.text: One found in plain overall in shift getting number for volume

indicators.note: in shift says the letters are moved into a new order
for says one letter is swapped in place of another

explanation.surface: A worker found on the plains in his overall, swapping the volume for a number.
explanation.walkthrough: OVERALL with N 'for' V gives ONERALL, rearranged 'in shift'.
explanation.definitionFit: A llanero is a herdsman or inhabitant of the llanos, the grassy plains of Venezuela and Colombia.

clue.text: Leading light in the past isn't prepared to follow etiquette (not half!)

indicators.note: to follow says the following letters come after the shortened etiquette
not half says only the first half of the word is kept

parts.note: protocol is official etiquette
ago means in the past

indicators.note: prepared says these letters are made ready in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone prominent who once was unwilling to observe etiquette, emphatically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is also British slang for 'very much'. 'prepared' rearranges ISNT to NIST.
explanation.definitionFit: The protagonist is the leading character or principal figure, the leading light of a story or cause.
